name: Philippines
headline: El Niño drought in the Philippines has become a declared disaster: as of 5 October 2026 states of calamity covered 106 areas in five regions, 388,375 people were affected and agricultural damage and losses reached PHP 5.56 billion, most of it in Cagayan Valley. PAGASA warns of a possibly record-breaking event lasting until March or even June 2027, with reduced rainfall expected to reach about 80 provinces by January. The drought follows a fuel and food price shock that pushed headline inflation to 7.2 per cent in April 2026, and the Philippines is the only country top-tier on both the 28 August regional snapshot and the IASC ENSO Cell lists.

other_lists: ACAPS: among countries at highest risk of severe humanitarian impacts, July 2026 – March 2027 (ACAPS, 7 Jul 2026)
FAO–WFP joint anticipatory-action appeal: one of four Asia-Pacific priority countries, with Afghanistan, Pakistan and Timor-Leste (FAO–WFP, 18 Jun 2026)
IFRC: one of sixteen countries particularly vulnerable because of high agricultural dependence (IFRC factsheet, produced Jul, published 21 Sep 2026)
June regional snapshot: Tier 2 — elevated, drier later 2026 / early 2027, impact window Jan–Apr 2027 (FAO/OCHA/WMO/WFP, 17 Jun 2026); superseded by the 28 Aug Tier 1
OCHA ROAP pre-onset list: high priority, dry conditions, through December 2026 (OCHA ROAP, 20 May 2026)
UNICEF: among countries expected to turn drier, with drought, water scarcity, displacement and acute-malnutrition risk (UNICEF EAPRO, 6 Oct 2026)
Historical susceptibility: very high on the drought side across eight El Niño/positive-IOD events, 1982–2024 (FAO/WFP/UN Women/WMO/OCHA snapshot, 28 Aug 2026)

hazard_outlook.text: PAGASA expects the event could reach very strong intensity in October–December (Climate Impact Outlook, Aug 2026); PAGASA's 22 July update favoured a very strong El Niño in Oct–Nov–Dec and Nov–Dec–Jan (~81%). The ECMWF SEAS5 forecast analysed by OCHA's Centre for Humanitarian Data projects the lowest Oct–Dec rainfall on record since 1981 (CERF secretariat, 30 Jun 2026).

Meteorological drought is expected from November, the month with the highest likelihood of drought development, especially in Luzon and the Visayas (Climate Impact Outlook, Aug 2026). PAGASA's June outlook projected about 45 provinces in dry condition or dry spell by end-November and about 81 by end-December (PAGASA, 22 Jun 2026).

Northern Luzon partly recovers as the Amihan (northeast monsoon) begins in December, while the Visayas and Mindanao stay dry (Climate Impact Outlook, Aug 2026). PAGASA expects reduced rainfall to reach about 80 provinces by January (PAGASA via GMA News, 6 Oct 2026).

PAGASA warned on 23 September of a possibly record-breaking El Niño lasting until March or even June 2027 (via GMA News, 6 Oct 2026); prolonged dry spells and droughts are highly likely in early 2027 (PAGASA via SCMP, 14 Jul 2026). The June regional snapshot placed the Philippine impact window at January–April 2027 (FAO/OCHA/WMO/WFP, 17 Jun 2026).

El Niño reduces the number of typhoons making Philippine landfall but increases their intensity (ACAPS, 7 Jul 2026); PAGASA warned of fewer but stronger typhoons on warmer seas (via The Philippine Star, 26 Jul 2026). Localised heavy rain and flooding remain likely in the western Philippines during the Habagat, Jul–Oct 2026 (Climate Impact Outlook, Aug 2026).

timeline.label: 13 May 2026
timeline.event: Nationwide 30-day retail price ceiling imposed on imported regular and well-milled rice; headline inflation eased from 6.8% (May) to 6.4% (June).

timeline.label: 9 Jun 2026
timeline.event: PAGASA El Niño Advisory: El Niño conditions present, >80% probability of a full El Niño likely to persist to early 2027.

timeline.label: 22 Jun 2026
timeline.event: PAGASA drought outlook: 17 provinces in drought and 34 in dry spell as of June 2026.

timeline.label: 23 Jun 2026
timeline.event: Magnitude-7.8 earthquake in Mindanao; recovery adds to the compounding hazards.
timeline.source: El Niño Climate Impact Outlook: Philippines (UN system)

timeline.label: 5 Jul 2026
timeline.event: Angat Dam, Metro Manila's main source, at 158.75 m, below its 160 m critical level; NWRB cut allocations from 52 to 48 cubic metres per second.

timeline.label: 13 Jul 2026
timeline.event: Tropical Cyclone Bavi and the enhanced southwest monsoon affected about 738,000 people across ten regions; 21 deaths, 8 injured, 16 missing and more than 15,000 displaced.

timeline.label: 1 Sep 2026
timeline.event: Transboundary haze from Kalimantan: 11 Metro Manila monitoring stations recorded 'acutely unhealthy' air.

timeline.label: 14 Sep 2026
timeline.event: MWSS cut Angat draws to ~42 cms from a historical 51–52 cms to build storage of 210–214 m by end-2026 ahead of the expected Q1 2027 dry spell.

timeline.label: 23 Sep 2026
timeline.event: PAGASA warned of a possibly record-breaking El Niño, with less rain from October and the event lasting until March or even June 2027.

timeline.label: 1 Oct 2026
timeline.event: Palace detailed response budget lines, including PHP 39.83 billion in the 2026 NDRRMF and PHP 6.2 billion for the Department of Agriculture; warned against hoarding of drinking water.

timeline.label: 5 Oct 2026
timeline.event: NDRRMC recorded states of calamity in 106 areas across five regions, with 388,375 people affected.

points: Agricultural damage and production losses reached PHP 5.56 billion, PHP 4.96 billion of it in Cagayan Valley; more than 223,497 ha of crops damaged, 41,164 ha with total loss (NDRRMC via GMA News, 6 Oct 2026).
First-quarter 2026 palay production fell 6.3% year on year to 4.4 million tonnes, the weakest start to a year since 2020 (PSA via SCMP, 14 Jul 2026).
USDA FAS cut MY2026/27 milled rice to 12.30 MMT (−0.8%) and corn to 8.10 MMT (−2.2%), raising rice imports to 5.20 MMT and corn imports 15% to 2.30 MMT (USDA FAS, 29 Jun 2026).
The Department of Agriculture projects a severe El Niño could cut national rice output by up to 700,000 tonnes (DA, May 2026, via SCMP, 14 Jul 2026).
Angat Dam fell to 158.75 m on 5 July, below its 160 m critical level; allocations to Metro Manila providers were cut from 52 to 48 cms (The Philippine Star, 26 Jul 2026).
By mid-September draws were cut to ~42 cms to bank water, targeting 210–214 m by end-2026 against the 160 m critical level (Manila Bulletin, 14 Sep 2026).
In Caraga, four cities and municipalities reported water-supply interruptions (NDRRMC via GMA News, 6 Oct 2026).
Headline inflation rose from 2.0% in January to 7.2% in April 2026, breaching the 2–4% target band, driven by transport (21.4%) and food (6.0%) (WFP, May 2026).
Food inflation was 4.60% year on year in August; on 28 September diesel was 64.5% and gasoline 60.8% above end-February (WFP Asia-Pacific, 5 Oct 2026).
ADB cut 2026 growth from 4.4% to 3.8%, the sharpest downgrade in its table, and raised 2026 inflation from 4.0% to 5.9% (ADB, Asian Development Outlook, Jul 2026).
33 localities in Caraga suspended classes (NDRRMC via GMA News, 6 Oct 2026).
In-person classes were cancelled in Cebu and parts of Manila and Luzon because of transboundary haze (TIME, 17 Sep 2026).

On 1 September, 11 Metro Manila stations recorded 'acutely unhealthy' air from Kalimantan smoke carried by the southwest monsoon; DENR and DOH advised limiting outdoor exposure and N95 masks (Rappler, 1 Sep 2026).
Smoke had reached as far as the Philippines in early October (China Daily/ANN, 15 Oct 2026).
Caraga recorded at least 39 wild, forest and mountain fires (NDRRMC via GMA News, 6 Oct 2026).
Measles transmission continued in the Philippines in the first half of 2026 (UNICEF EAPRO, 30 Jun 2026).
PAGASA flagged nighttime temperatures rising faster than daytime highs and heat-index values approaching 40 °C in Cagayan Valley (Southeast Asia Desk, 16 Apr 2026).
The Philippines is one of nine contexts in the region holding El Niño-specific GBV risk analysis; all contexts anticipate increased GBV risk (GBV Coordination Asia Pacific/REGA, Q2 2026).
UNICEF names the Philippines among countries expected to turn drier, with risks of displacement, acute malnutrition, school dropout, child labour and child marriage (UNICEF EAPRO, 6 Oct 2026).

An El Niño action plan was activated in May 2026; the DA reactivated its El Niño Task Force and set out PHP 1 billion in farmer and fisherfolk aid and PHP 1.6 billion for solar irrigation (The Philippine Star, 26 Jul 2026).

For 2026, PHP 39.83 billion is in the NDRRMF and PHP 6.2 billion earmarked for the DA; the proposed 2027 budget carries PHP 45.67 billion for the NDRRMF and PHP 11.18 billion for NFA rice buffer stocking (The Manila Times, 1 Oct 2026).

A fixed-price agreement with Viet Nam covers 1.5 million tonnes of rice imports through April 2027 (FAO GIEWS FPMA, 30 Jun 2026); excise taxes on LPG and kerosene were suspended for three months (WFP Asia-Pacific, 5 Oct 2026).
Assistance delivered as of 5 October totalled PHP 39,058,681 (NDRRMC via GMA News, 6 Oct 2026); farm groups describe implementation as 'all talk' (SCMP, 14 Jul 2026).
The Philippines is an Asia-Pacific priority country in the FAO–WFP joint anticipatory-action appeal of US$202 million for 8.8 million people in 22 countries (FAO–WFP, 18 Jun 2026).

The Red Cross holds a simplified Early Action Protocol for cyclones in the Philippines (MDRPH055), with trigger monitoring, readiness and prepositioning under way; no drought protocol is active in Asia-Pacific (IFRC, 6 Jul 2026).
UNICEF is piloting an automated e-SitRep system in the Philippines ahead of regional rollout (UNICEF EAPRO, 30 Jun 2026).

CERF's Philippine anticipatory-action framework covers tropical cyclones, US$6,000,000 pre-arranged, status under revision; no drought framework exists in the Asia-Pacific El Niño-relevant set (CERF secretariat, 30 Jun 2026).

ADB approved US$750 million for the Build Universal Health Care Program, raised by US$250 million as oil price and supply shocks widened financing needs, with about US$188 million JICA cofinancing (ADB, 11 Aug 2026).

history: 2023–24: 37 provinces in drought at the March 2024 peak, states of calamity in 5 provinces and 34 LGUs, and 531,000 families / 2.28 million people affected across 3,053 villages in 11 regions (ACT Alliance citing DSWD DROMIC, 2024); farm losses estimated at PHP 57.78 billion (PSA via The Philippine Star, 26 Jul 2026).

2015–16: a prolonged dry spell compounded by erratic tropical storms affected over 2.1 million people (457,497 families), 181,687 farmers and 224,834 ha of agricultural land (OCHA ROAP, 20 May 2026); drought plus rat and pest outbreaks cut yields 30–40% in some severely affected areas (Climate Impact Outlook, Aug 2026).
1997–98: the super El Niño triggered a 22% collapse in palay production (SCMP, 14 Jul 2026) and a record 1.35 million tonnes of rice imports (Climate Impact Outlook, Aug 2026).

Across 1997–98, 2015–16 and 2023–24 the strongest recurrence of impacts was in south-central and western Mindanao (Cotabato, Maguindanao, Sarangani, Sultan Kudarat), with repeat impacts in Central Luzon, Western Visayas, northern Luzon and MIMAROPA (Climate Impact Outlook, Aug 2026).
cautions: The 28 Aug regional snapshot's Philippines paragraph gives 'more than 107,000 hectares burned by 11 August' and 'more than 5,000 fire hotspots'; the wiki identifies these as Indonesian figures placed under the wrong country, and they are not used here as Philippine data.

Estimates of El Niño's effect on Philippine inflation disagree: Bloomberg Economics puts it at +1.85 percentage points (5 Aug 2026), Allianz Research at +0.7 pp, calling the Philippines 'most insulated' (16 Jul 2026); the wiki notes the impact is uncertain by more than a percentage point.
2023–24 agricultural losses differ by source: PHP 57.78 billion (PSA via The Philippine Star, 26 Jul 2026) against 'national losses exceeding PHP 15 billion' (Climate Impact Outlook, Aug 2026).

UNICEF's mid-year report gives more than 1.6 million people affected by earthquakes in June 2026, and elsewhere in the same report around 1.9 million affected by a major earthquake over the period (UNICEF EAPRO, 30 Jun 2026).

IFRC's factsheet lists the Philippines under increased rainfall and flooding, while every seasonal product places it on the dry side; the wiki reads this as sub-national or cyclone-season flood exposure, not a wet seasonal signal. The Climate Impact Outlook also notes the WMO >90% figure is the probability that El Niño persists, not of drought in the Philippines.
